title: Reported speech
intro: Reported speech tells another person what someone said. At B1 you change statements and questions; at B2 you also use a wider choice of reporting verbs.

sources.label: British Council: Reported speech: reporting verbs

sections.title: Reported statements
sections.summary: When you report what someone said, you usually move the verb one step back in time.

tables.caption: Tense changes
head: direct speech
reported speech
rows: past simple: She said she worked here.
past continuous: He said he was waiting.
past perfect: She said she had finished.
past perfect: He said he had seen it.
would: She said she would help.
could: He said he could swim.

uses: Say and tell: say something (to someone), tell someone something. She told me that she was tired.
That is optional: He said (that) he was ill.
Change pronouns and time words: today becomes that day, tomorrow becomes the next day, here becomes there, now becomes then.
You do not have to change the tense when the fact is still true: She said she lives in Paris.

examples.text: "I am tired." She said that she was tired.
"We will call you." They told me they would call me.
"I visited Rome last year." He said he had visited Rome the year before.
examples.note: Past simple moves to past perfect.

mistakes.wrong: She told that she was ill.
mistakes.right: She told me that she was ill. / She said that she was ill.
mistakes.why: Tell needs a person after it.

mistakes.wrong: He said me he was tired.
mistakes.right: He told me he was tired.
mistakes.why: Say does not take a person without to.

mistakes.wrong: She said she is coming tomorrow.
mistakes.right: She said she was coming the next day.
mistakes.why: Backshift and change the time word.

checks.question: Report: "I like pizza." (She said)
checks.explanation: Present simple moves to past simple.

checks.question: Report: "I have lost my keys." (He said)
checks.answer: He said he had lost his keys.
checks.explanation: Present perfect moves to past perfect.

sections.title: Reported questions
sections.summary: In reported questions the word order is the same as in a statement. There is no auxiliary do and no question mark.

tables.caption: Reported questions
head: direct question
reported question
rows: She asked me where I lived.
He asked what time it started.
She asked if I was ready.
He asked whether I had seen it.

uses: Use if or whether for yes / no questions.
Use the same wh- word for other questions: where, when, what, why, how.
Use the word order of a statement: subject then verb.
Backshift the tense in the same way as for statements.
Ask is the usual verb; add me / him / her if you want: He asked me where I lived.

examples.text: "Why are you late?" She asked me why I was late.
"Do you speak French?" He asked if I spoke French.
She wondered whether it would rain.
examples.note: Wonder + whether is a reported question.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
mistakes.right: He asked me where I lived.
mistakes.why: No do and no question word order.

mistakes.wrong: She asked did I like it.
mistakes.right: She asked if I liked it.

mistakes.wrong: He asked what was my name.
mistakes.right: He asked what my name was.
mistakes.why: Statement word order: subject then verb.

checks.question: Report: "Where is the station?" (She asked me)
checks.answer: She asked me where the station was.

checks.question: Report: "Do you like jazz?" (He asked me)
checks.answer: He asked me if I liked jazz.
checks.explanation: Use if for yes / no questions.

sections.title: Reporting verbs
sections.summary: Many verbs report not only the words but also the purpose of what someone said.

tables.caption: Patterns after reporting verbs
head: pattern
verbs
example
rows: He admitted that he was wrong.
advise, ask, invite, order, remind, tell, warn
She advised me to see a doctor.
apologise for, insist on, complain about

uses: A reporting verb is shorter and more exact than said.
Direct speech: "Don't touch it!" Reported: He warned me not to touch it.
Suggest takes -ing or a that clause: She suggested going / that we go. Do not use suggest + to.
After promise you can use a that clause or an infinitive: He promised to call / that he would call.

examples.text: "You should rest." The doctor advised me to rest.
"I'll help you." He offered to help me.
She apologised for forgetting my birthday.

mistakes.right: He suggested going. / He suggested that I go.

checks.question: Report with a verb: "I'll carry it," he said.
Report with a verb: "Don't forget your keys," she said to me.
checks.answer: She reminded me not to forget my keys.
